new_packages.label: מֹשֶׁה מָשִׁיחַ וְהַצַּדִּיק
new_packages.label_en: Moshe, Mashiach, and the True Tzaddik

concepts.bechina_phrase: יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִדָּה שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה
כָּל צַדִּיק... יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִדָּה שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
דָּא מֹשֶׁה מָשִׁיחַ, דְּאִתְמַר בֵּהּ: וּמַטֵּה הָאֱלֹקִים בְּיָדִי. מַטֶּה דָּא מְט"ט

new_packages.reason: The Torah opens with the equation: every true Tzaddik contains a dimension of Mashiach, and Mashiach is a bechina of Moshe (Zohar: 'מָשִׁיחַ דָּא מֹשֶׁה'). The state of complete teshuvah is itself called 'בְּחִינוֹת מֹשֶׁה מָשִׁיחַ' (line 14, 17). All three — Tzaddik, Mashiach, Moshe — share the same essential nature: the leader who surrenders his life for Israel (מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ), who knows his own lowliness (שִׁפְלוּת), and who can turn evil to good. מַטֵּה הָאֱלֹקִים is a bechina of מֹשֶׁה מָשִׁיחַ in the Zohar passage quoted, which is why it appears here. The Torah explicitly bridges this cluster to the שַׁבָּת cluster (complete teshuvah = Moshe-Mashiach state), so this package is connected to Package 1 via eitza but has its own independent bechina domain. None of these nodes appear in the bechina dataset for Torah 79.
new_packages.note: The מַטֵּה הָאֱלֹקִים / מַטֶּה דָּא מְט"ט equivalence links this cluster to the existing מט"ט node in Package 1. This is a structural bridge where מֹשֶׁה מָשִׁיחַ (the person / the state) connects to מט"ט (the Kabbalistic principle). Both are expressions of the staff-of-transformation ('מִסִּטְרֵהּ חַיִּים וּמִסִּטְרֵהּ מִיתָה').

new_packages.label: שִׁפְלוּת וְאַיִן

concepts.bechina_phrase: שֶׁפּוֹגֵם בִּבְחִינַת עֲנָוָה וְשִׁפְלוּת, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת: שְׁבוּ אִישׁ תַּחְתָּיו
הוּא עָנָו וְשָׁפָל בֶּאֱמֶת, הוּא בִּבְחִינַת אַיִן
שִׁפְלוּת הַנַּ"ל, בְּחִינַת: שְׁבוּ אִישׁ תַּחְתָּיו

new_packages.reason: The second half of the Torah (lines 24–27) introduces an independent conceptual domain: true humility (שִׁפְלוּת/עֲנָוָה) as the quality of self-nullification (אַיִן). The verse 'שְׁבוּ אִישׁ תַּחְתָּיו' is explicitly identified as a bechina of שִׁפְלוּת/עֲנָוָה. The one who is truly humble is 'in a bechina of אַיִן' — he does not occupy any place in the spatial/competitive sense, and therefore no one can displace him from his livelihood. These four concepts (שִׁפְלוּת, עֲנָוָה, אַיִן, שְׁבוּ אִישׁ תַּחְתָּיו) form a tight bechina cluster sharing the essential nature of self-nullification/non-occupancy. This is an independent domain not fully covered by Package 1 (which covers the completeness/rest state of teshuvah, not the quality of humility as such). None of these nodes appear in the bechina dataset for Torah 79.
new_packages.note: This package connects to Package 1 via eitza (complete teshuvah leads to seeing one's שִׁפְלוּת, which is the שַׁבָּת dimension). And it connects to Package 79-NEW-1 via eitza (Moshe's שִׁפְלוּת is what enabled him to give his life for Israel). But the bechina domain of שִׁפְלוּת/אַיִן is structurally independent: it answers 'what IS humility at its core?' — nothingness/non-place — which is different from answering 'what IS complete teshuvah?'

observations: Torah #79 is a compact teaching organized around two primary conceptual poles that are structurally connected but thematically distinct. The bechina dataset captures only the central theological core (7 edges: the שַׁבָּת/שַׁדַּי/מט"ט/מִשְׁנָה axis). However, the source text contains at least two additional independent bechina domains that are entirely absent from the dataset: (1) the Tzaddik/Moshe/Mashiach cluster — the human embodiment of the complete-teshuvah state, and (2) the שִׁפְלוּת/אַיִן cluster — the mechanism by which one achieves true humility. The absence of these clusters from the dataset represents a significant gap in Torah 79's bechina coverage. The מֹשֶׁה/מָשִׁיחַ cluster is particularly important because the Torah opens and closes with it, and it serves as the bridge between the theoretical (שַׁבָּת state) and the practical (the Tzaddik who achieves it and transmits it). The שִׁפְלוּת/אַיִן cluster generates the practical application (second half of the Torah, lines 24–27) and is linked by the enigmatic rabbinic statement about entering a colleague's livelihood as equivalent to violating a married woman (line 27).
